newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates dip on money shortage.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates dip on money shortage.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates dipped on Sunday because of low buying interest by spinners owing to a paucity of funds and the year-end holiday season, dealers said.

All the three main varieties quoted by the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) in its daily official spot rates fell 27.50 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) in dull trading, broker Khushi Ram said. The spinners had already bought enough stocks of cotton and delayed further purchases until January.
In the kerb market, the rate for NIAB-78 variety remained between 2,325 and 2,350 rupees per maund, he said.
